models.name: Storm Intensity Distribution
models.description: Hybrid Normal-Pareto distribution for storm rainfall intensity modelling. Uses Gaussian core with Generalised Pareto Distribution (GPD) tail above a fitted threshold.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: feeds into downstream hazard models but not directly into pricing. Medium complexity: hybrid distribution with threshold selection requiring expert judgement.
models.methodology: Hybrid Normal-GPD with maximum likelihood threshold estimation
models.methodology_rationale: Hybrid approach captures both typical and extreme rainfall. Pure Pareto overestimates body; lognormal underestimates tail. GPD-only misses the distribution body needed for moderate events.

assumptions.description: Storm events are independent
assumptions.monitoring: Check autocorrelation in residuals
assumptions.mitigation: Seasonal decomposition if violated

assumptions.description: Stationarity of rainfall distribution
assumptions.monitoring: Rolling parameter stability test
assumptions.mitigation: Climate trend adjustment

assumptions.description: No spatial correlation between storm intensities
assumptions.monitoring: Cross-site correlation analysis
assumptions.mitigation: Copula extension if needed

assumptions.description: GPD threshold selection is appropriate
assumptions.monitoring: Mean residual life plot stability
assumptions.mitigation: Sensitivity analysis on threshold

limitations.description: Independence assumption may not hold for clustered storm events
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Autocorrelation > 0.3 at lag 1
limitations.compensating_control: Manual review of clustered events

limitations.description: Stationarity assumption ignores climate change trends
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Significant trend in 10-year rolling parameters
limitations.compensating_control: Annual recalibration with trend test

limitations.description: No spatial correlation modelled
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Portfolio concentration in single catchment
limitations.compensating_control: Diversification requirement

limitations.description: Threshold selection involves subjective judgement
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Threshold sensitivity > 10% on tail quantiles
limitations.compensating_control: Document threshold selection rationale

known_failure_modes: Very small sample sizes (<20 events) cause unstable GPD fit
Bimodal rainfall distributions (convective + frontal) poorly captured by single hybrid
Extreme extrapolation beyond observed data unreliable

models.output_data: Storm intensity probability distribution, exceedance probabilities

models.name: Storm-Gauge Response Model
models.description: Spatial decay model mapping storm intensity to gauge-level water levels. Uses distance-based attenuation with catchment-specific calibration.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: translates storm events to local water levels for downstream GEV fitting. Medium complexity: spatial interpolation with calibrated decay parameters.
models.methodology: Spatial decay with distance-based intensity-to-level conversion
models.methodology_rationale: Physical decay model is interpretable and auditable. Kriging requires more data points than typically available. Neural networks lack transparency for regulatory purposes.

assumptions.description: No antecedent moisture conditions modelled
assumptions.monitoring: Compare predicted vs observed for wet/dry antecedent periods
assumptions.mitigation: Seasonal adjustment factor

assumptions.description: Linear storm track interpolation

assumptions.mitigation: Higher-order interpolation if needed

assumptions.description: Static decay parameters
assumptions.monitoring: Parameter stability across seasons
assumptions.mitigation: Seasonal recalibration

assumptions.description: No tidal interaction
assumptions.monitoring: Residual analysis for coastal gauges
assumptions.mitigation: Tidal correction for estuarine gauges

limitations.description: No antecedent conditions modelling
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Systematic under-prediction after prolonged wet periods
limitations.compensating_control: Seasonal moisture index adjustment

limitations.description: Linear track interpolation may miss curved storm paths
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Track error > 10km at gauge locations
limitations.compensating_control: Manual track review for significant events

limitations.description: Static sensitivity parameters
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Parameter drift > 15% over 12 months

limitations.description: No tidal interaction for coastal/estuarine gauges

limitations.compensating_control: Exclude estuarine gauges or add tidal overlay

known_failure_modes: Gauges in urban areas with complex drainage may not follow spatial decay assumptions
Flash flood events with very localised intensity poorly modelled by regional decay
Snow-melt driven floods not captured by rainfall-only model

models.name: GEV Hazard Curve Model
models.description: Generalised Extreme Value distribution fitting for flood exceedance rates. Constructs hazard curves showing probability of exceeding given flood depths at each gauge location.
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: directly determines flood exceedance probabilities used in pricing and capital. High complexity: GEV fitting with shape parameter estimation, return level extrapolation, and term structure construction.
models.methodology: Maximum likelihood GEV fitting with exceedance rate scaling and return level term structure
models.methodology_rationale: GEV is the theoretically justified distribution for block maxima (annual maximum flood levels). GPD requires threshold selection; empirical methods cannot extrapolate; Log-Pearson less flexible shape.

assumptions.description: Annual maxima are independent and identically distributed
assumptions.monitoring: Ljung-Box test on annual maxima series
assumptions.mitigation: Time-varying GEV parameters

assumptions.description: Stationarity over the observation period
assumptions.monitoring: Mann-Kendall trend test on annual maxima
assumptions.mitigation: Non-stationary GEV extension

assumptions.description: Univariate analysis per gauge (no spatial dependence)
assumptions.monitoring: Cross-gauge correlation analysis
assumptions.mitigation: Max-stable process extension

assumptions.description: Exceedance probability scaled by base flood rate
assumptions.monitoring: Base rate stability over time
assumptions.mitigation: Recalibrate base rate annually

limitations.description: Sample size sensitivity: <30 annual maxima gives unstable shape parameter
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Shape parameter confidence interval width > 0.3
limitations.compensating_control: Regional frequency analysis or Bayesian prior

limitations.description: Stationarity assumption may not hold under climate change
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Significant trend (p<0.05) in annual maxima
limitations.compensating_control: Climate-adjusted return levels

limitations.description: Univariate analysis ignores spatial flood dependence
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Correlated gauge failures in same event
limitations.compensating_control: Portfolio-level spatial diversification check

known_failure_modes: Very short records (<15 years) produce unreliable extreme quantiles
Mixed flood generation mechanisms (pluvial + fluvial + tidal) violate iid assumption
Shape parameter > 0.5 indicates heavy tail that may be physically unrealistic
models.input_data: Per-gauge water level time series (from MKM-SG-001 or historical observations)
models.output_data: Hazard curves (exceedance probability vs flood depth), return levels, term structure

models.name: PRS Analytical Pricing Model
models.description: Analytical Physical Risk Swap spread calculation using hazard curve exceedance probabilities. Computes fair swap spreads for flood protection at gauge and property levels, with basis analysis.
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: directly determines PRS swap spreads used in trading and risk transfer. High complexity: credit-curve-style pricing with multiple depth thresholds, term structure, and basis waterfall decomposition.
models.methodology: Analytical spread from hazard curve exceedance rates with 5-component basis waterfall
models.methodology_rationale: Analytical approach is transparent, fast, and auditable. QuantLib CDS available as benchmark but adds dependency. Monte Carlo unnecessary for current product complexity. Simple expected loss ignores term structure.

assumptions.description: Zero recovery assumption on flood events
assumptions.monitoring: Compare with actual recovery rates when data available
assumptions.mitigation: Recovery rate sensitivity analysis

assumptions.description: Flat risk-free curve
assumptions.monitoring: Interest rate curve steepness
assumptions.mitigation: Term-structure-aware discounting

assumptions.description: Quarterly discretisation of protection periods
assumptions.monitoring: Discretisation error vs monthly calculation
assumptions.mitigation: Move to monthly if error > 5bps

assumptions.description: No correlation between flood events at different properties
assumptions.monitoring: Portfolio-level concentration metrics
assumptions.mitigation: Correlation haircut for concentrated portfolios

limitations.description: Zero-recovery assumption overstates spread for moderate floods
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Spread deviation from QuantLib benchmark > 20bps
limitations.compensating_control: Recovery rate overlay for moderate depth thresholds

limitations.description: Flat risk-free curve ignores term structure effects
limitations.monitoring_trigger: 2s10s curve steepness > 200bps
limitations.compensating_control: QuantLib benchmark with full curve

limitations.description: Quarterly discretisation introduces small pricing error
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Error vs monthly > 5bps
limitations.compensating_control: Increase to monthly frequency

limitations.description: No correlation modelling between properties
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Portfolio HHI > 0.3
limitations.compensating_control: Diversification benefit cap

known_failure_modes: Very low exceedance probabilities (<0.01%) produce numerically unstable spreads
Basis waterfall can produce negative basis for highly concentrated portfolios
Short-term contracts (<1yr) may have insufficient premium to cover fixed costs
models.input_data: Hazard curves (from MKM-GH-001), property locations, depth-damage curves
models.output_data: PRS fair spread (bps), term structure of spreads, basis waterfall components

models.name: Depth-Damage Curve Model
models.description: Piecewise linear depth-damage functions mapping flood depth to property damage ratio. Supports multiple property types with calibrated damage curves.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: determines damage ratios used in portfolio loss calculations. Low complexity: piecewise linear interpolation with published damage curves.
models.methodology: Piecewise linear interpolation from published depth-damage tables
models.methodology_rationale: Piecewise linear is transparent, matches published industry tables, and avoids overfitting. Polynomial fits can produce non-monotonic artifacts. ML approaches lack interpretability.

assumptions.description: Damage depends only on depth (not velocity or duration)
assumptions.monitoring: Compare with multi-factor models where data available
assumptions.mitigation: Velocity adjustment for high-flow areas

assumptions.description: Published damage curves are representative of UK properties
assumptions.monitoring: Actual loss data comparison when available
assumptions.mitigation: Regional calibration

limitations.description: Single-factor model ignores velocity and duration effects

limitations.compensating_control: Velocity factor overlay for known high-flow areas

limitations.description: Curves based on published averages, not property-specific

limitations.compensating_control: Property-type-specific curve selection

known_failure_modes: Negative flood depths (basement flooding) not modelled
Very deep flooding (>3m) extrapolated beyond calibration range

models.name: Spatial Interpolation Model
models.description: Inverse Distance Weighting interpolation for mapping gauge observations to property locations. Uses KDTree for efficient nearest-neighbour search with configurable power parameter.
models.tier_rationale: Low materiality: supporting calculation that maps gauge data to properties. Low complexity: well-established IDW algorithm with standard implementation.
models.methodology: Inverse Distance Weighting with KDTree nearest-neighbour search and Haversine distance
models.methodology_rationale: IDW provides smooth interpolation without requiring variogram estimation. Computationally efficient for real-time use. Kriging would require more gauge density than available.

assumptions.description: Spatial field is smooth between gauge locations
assumptions.monitoring: Cross-validation leave-one-out error
assumptions.mitigation: Increase gauge density

assumptions.description: Haversine distance is appropriate for distances < 50km
assumptions.monitoring: N/A - always valid at catchment scale
assumptions.mitigation: N/A

limitations.description: IDW cannot extrapolate beyond gauge network convex hull
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Properties outside gauge network
limitations.compensating_control: Flag extrapolated properties

limitations.description: Isotropic weighting ignores terrain effects
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Large elevation differences between gauge and property
limitations.compensating_control: Elevation-adjusted distance metric

known_failure_modes: Properties very close to a single gauge get dominated by that gauge
Properties equidistant from gauges with very different readings produce averaged values

models.output_data: Interpolated values at property locations

models.name: Property Valuation Model
models.description: Factor-based property valuation using area, price/sqm, age, condition, flood risk, EPC rating, and proximity adjustments.

models.name: Delta Engine
models.description: PRS trade revaluation engine computing FS01 (Flood Sensitivity 01), mark-to-market, risky annuity, and portfolio risk grid aggregation. Uses numerical bump-and-reprice on the analytical PRS pricing model.
models.tier_rationale: High materiality: directly drives P&L, risk limits, and position management for the PRS trading desk. Medium complexity: standard bump-and-reprice approach using established pricing functions.
models.methodology: Numerical bump-and-reprice delta with quarterly risky annuity and yield-curve-matched discounting
models.methodology_rationale: Numerical delta via 1bp bump is standard practice for credit derivatives risk. Consistent with the discrete-time pricing model. Analytical delta would require separate derivation and maintenance.

assumptions.description: Parallel hazard rate bump for FS01 (no curve risk)
assumptions.monitoring: Compare FS01 prediction to actual revaluation P&L
assumptions.mitigation: Full revaluation available for P&L verification

assumptions.description: Constant basis for property trades under small gauge rate moves
assumptions.monitoring: Track basis stability vs gauge rate changes
assumptions.mitigation: Full basis recalculation for large moves

assumptions.description: Independent gauge moves (no cross-gamma)
assumptions.monitoring: Portfolio concentration limits by gauge
assumptions.mitigation: Stress testing with correlated scenarios

limitations.description: First-order sensitivity only; no gamma/convexity for large moves
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Unexplained P&L residual > 10% of daily P&L
limitations.compensating_control: Full revaluation check on material moves

limitations.description: No yield curve sensitivity (IR DV01)
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Yield curve moves > 50bp in a day
limitations.compensating_control: Yield curve is trader-controlled, moves are deliberate

limitations.description: No jump risk modelling for catastrophic events
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Hazard rate jump > 100bp intraday
limitations.compensating_control: Position limits and notional caps

known_failure_modes: Very high hazard rates (>10%) cause nonlinear spread behaviour not captured by 1bp bump
Zero-tenor trades (expired) return degenerate delta values
Missing market state file causes fallback to flat 4% rate
models.input_data: PRS trade files (CDM format), market_state.json (yield curve, hazard term structures)
models.output_data: Enriched trade records with MTM, FS01, fair spread, risky annuity; risk grid

models.name: Storm Sequence Generator
models.description: Multi-storm sequence generator implementing the insurance hours clause (168-hour event window). Produces catalogues of 1-5 related precipitation events (isolated, doublet, cluster, persistent) using budget-based window fitting, triangular duration/gap distributions, and correlated intensity sampling. v2.0 upgrade; replaces single-storm paradigm for stress testing. Trains stressm flood classifiers achieving mean AUC ~0.993.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: primary training data source for stressm flood classifier (MKM-FC-001 v2.0) which feeds Portfolio Stress P&L. Medium complexity: sequence type selection, budget-based timing constraints, correlated intensity sampling within sequences.
models.methodology: Triangular distribution sampling with deterministic budget-cap and proportional gap scaling
models.methodology_rationale: Budget-cap + proportional gap scaling guarantees every sequence fits the event window in O(1) without rejection loops or fallbacks. Rejection sampling (v1.x) produced >20% fallback rate for catastrophic sequences corrupting the type distribution. Markov chains add unnecessary complexity for a training-data generator. Empirical catalogues are too sparse for 10,000-sequence batches.

models.name: Flood Polynomial Model
models.description: Logistic sigmoid with quadratic polynomial kernel approximating the GBM flood classifier. Maps log-space water level ln(w/s) and storm time ln((t+1)/T) to P(flood) via six fitted coefficients. R²=0.94 against the full GBM surface. Used for portfolio stress (time-independent variant) and single-gauge stress scenarios.
models.tier_rationale: Low materiality: approximation of existing GBM classifier for portfolio-level stress. Low complexity: closed-form logistic sigmoid with 6 fixed coefficients, no training required.
models.methodology: Nonlinear least-squares fit of logistic sigmoid to GBM probability surface
models.methodology_rationale: Quadratic sigmoid captures the essential water level × time interaction with only 6 parameters. Linear interpolation loses the time dimension; step functions create discontinuities; cubic adds marginal accuracy (MAE 0.033 vs 0.046) with more parameters; full GBM requires per-gauge trained models which are not always available.

models.name: Building Resilience Index (BRI) Model
models.description: Property resilience assessment with two co-located outputs: (1) BRI letter rating (AA / AA+ / A / A+ / B / B+ / NR) derived via weakest-link aggregation across applicable hazards from a 5-level resilience checklist, and (2) Flood resilience score (1-100) per the IFC BRI Resilience Function Specification — a weighted 13-measure model with regime multipliers, soft caps, and a linear damage modifier intended to scale an existing flood damage function.
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: produces resilience ratings and scores that feed downstream consumers (governance reporting, insurance ratings, future damage-function scaling) but does not currently enter pricing directly. High complexity: two related-but-distinct scoring paradigms (categorical weakest-link letter rating + continuous weighted-measure score with soft caps), Thames-specific calibrated weights, 13-measure compliance mapping with mixed continuous/ordinal/binary inputs, regime-specific weight multipliers.
models.methodology: Two co-located methodologies. (1) BRI letter rating: per-hazard score from 5-level resilience checklist (Not assessed=0, Partial=0.4, Meets minimum=0.7, Enhanced=0.9, Verified=1.0) weighted by section + per-field weights; overall letter is weakest-of applicable hazards with '+' modifier when ContinuityMeasures section score >= 0.65. (2) Flood resilience score: per-spec 13 weighted measures (sum to 100), regime-specific weight multipliers (pluvial / fluvial / coastal), four soft-cap rules, linear damage modifier M(S,r) = 1 - alpha_r * (S-1)/99 with alpha = {0.65, 0.60, 0.50}.
alternatives_considered: Pure weakest-link letter rating only (rejected: loses score granularity for portfolio analytics)
Continuous score only without letter rating (rejected: letter scale needed for human-readable disclosure)
Single-paradigm hybrid where letter is derived from score thresholds (deferred: requires calibration data not yet available)
Per-property location-context normalisation (deferred: design under review)
models.methodology_rationale: The letter rating mirrors IFC BRI public methodology and produces an auditable, disclosable grade. The continuous score provides the precision needed for loss-given-hazard scaling and portfolio aggregation. Co-locating them in one module gives a single source of truth for resilience analytics. Thames-specific weights reflect the dominant fluvial flood hazard in the catchment; other catchments would have their own copy.

assumptions.monitoring: Inter-rater agreement studies on a sample portfolio
assumptions.mitigation: Reference photos and worked examples per measure; assessor calibration training

models.name: BRI-Adjusted Floor Level Model
models.description: Translates a property's BRI flood resilience score into an additive uplift on its surveyed floor level, raising the effective flood threshold used by the PRS event filter. A highly resilient building (raised thresholds, barriers, flood-proof construction) only counts as flooded once water rises well above its nominal floor, suppressing severe-flood counts and thereby lowering its PRS flood spread. This model realises the BRI-OA3 wiring of BRI resilience into pricing via the floor-uplift route (rather than the deferred damage-modifier route).
models.tier_rationale: Medium materiality: the uplift directly reduces PRS flood-count and therefore the priced 'resilient' spread that feeds MKM-PR-001 and the loan calculator's flood leg, but only for the optional resilient PRS variant alongside the unchanged 'pure' variant. Medium complexity: a single continuous, monotone, additive ramp with three calibration anchors and a letter-grade fallback table; no interacting caps or regime logic.
models.methodology: Additive floor uplift. uplift(s) is a continuous, monotone ramp in the BRIFloodScore s in [0,1]: uplift = 0 for s <= SCORE_LO (0.38, NR/B boundary), uplift = MAX_M (3.00 m) for s >= SCORE_HI (0.87, AA anchor), and linearly interpolated in between. The effective flood-threshold floor is adjusted_floor = FloorLevelMeters + uplift(s). An event floods the property iff attenuated_wse_m > GroundLevelMeters + adjusted_floor. The uplift is always >= 0 (a poor BRI score never lowers the threshold below the surveyed floor; below-reference vulnerability is expressed by the separate depth-damage stilt, not here). Assets carrying a BRI letter grade rather than a numeric flood score (e.g. commercial) map the grade to a representative score via BRI_FLOOR_RATING_SCORES (band mid-points: AA 0.935, A 0.745, B 0.500, NR 0.190) before the ramp is evaluated.
alternatives_considered: Subtractive penalty for low BRI (rejected: floor uplift is a resilience credit; vulnerability is already handled by the depth-damage stilt)
Step function by letter grade (rejected: discontinuous spread jumps at grade boundaries; continuous-from-score chosen)

Multiplicative scaling of the damage modifier M(S,r) instead of a floor uplift (deferred as BRI-OA3 Phase 2; floor-uplift route chosen first because it maps cleanly onto the PRS severe-flood-count filter)
Overwriting the canonical PRS term structure with the BRI-adjusted spread (rejected: would lose the pure surveyed-floor spread; pure + resilient variants are booked side by side instead)
models.methodology_rationale: The PRS flood spread is driven by a severe-flood count over a fixed storm set (spread_bps = flood_count / num_storms x 10000). Raising the effective floor can only remove events from the count (strict subset), so the BRI-adjusted ('resilient') spread is always <= the surveyed-floor ('pure') spread; resilience_effect_bps = pure_spread - bri_spread >= 0 is a monotone invariant. An additive, continuous uplift anchored on the published BRIFloodScore grade bands gives an auditable, smoothly-varying resilience credit without introducing discontinuities at grade boundaries.

models.name: Wind Damage
models.description: Per-property damage ratio from peak sustained wind during a typhoon event. Mirrors the flood-damage architecture: a pure piecewise saturated sigmoid plus a BRI-aware wrapper that shifts the curve's v_50 by a log-aggregated function of BRIWindScore and the composite BRIScore. Consumes the per-event wind timeseries produced by MKM-TC-001 + MKM-WS-001. A persistence (duration-of-load) factor now scales the peak-curve damage by how long the sustained wind stayed above the property’s v_50_eff, so a single gust is less damaging than the same peak sustained for hours.
models.tier_rationale: Low complexity: closed-form sigmoid + log-aggregated shift. Medium materiality: feeds property / commercial damage estimates directly, parallel to MKM-DD-001 for flood.
models.methodology: DR(v) = 1 / (1 + exp(-a * (v - v_50))). v_50 from CDM WindThresholdKph (default 100 kph) shifted by alpha*ln(bri_wind/ref) + beta*ln(bri_composite/ref) in m/s, capped. Persistence: DR = peak_curve(v) x Phi(t), with Phi(t) = phi_gust + (1 - phi_gust)*(1 - exp(-t/tau)) and t = hours sustained wind exceeded v_50_eff. The peak-only curve is the t->inf saturated bound.
alternatives_considered: Power-law: DR = k*(v-v0)^p (rejected: harder to bound to [0,1] without ad-hoc clipping)
Empirical lookup table (deferred: needs calibration data)
Duration-aware integrated dose (alternative to the adopted saturating duration-of-load factor; revisit at calibration)
models.methodology_rationale: Sigmoid is bounded to [0,1] by construction, monotonic, symmetric about v_50, and well-understood. Per-property v_50 from the CDM lets calibration analysts tune the threshold without touching the model. BRI integration mirrors flood's stilt for architectural consistency. The saturating persistence factor captures the duration-of-load effect (fatigue / prolonged debris loading) while staying bounded and reducing to the peak-only curve when sustained, so the two families remain consistent.

models.name: Building Fire-Resilience Credit Model
models.description: Prices the fire-resilience of a commercial asset so fire loss aggregates into the same resilience-credit currency as the storm and typhoon hazards. Built from four governance-separated component models: A (Poisson ignition frequency), B (deterministic 15-minute latent intensity track), C (CDM resilience levels -> response dynamics), and D (an 8-state discrete-time Bayesian containment chain). The central concept is the point of no return: the first step at which latent intensity exceeds a critical threshold before suppression bites, after which the chain switches to an absorbing matrix whose Contained column is zero. Outputs an unconditional annual loss frequency and a fire-conditional containment rate.
models.tier_rationale: Materiality TBD: the fire-resilience credit is intended to feed PRS-style pricing pari-passu with the flood and wind legs, but is not yet wired into the pricing chain, so its priced impact is not yet realised. High complexity: a four-stage pipeline combining Poisson initiation, a deterministic intensity track, a controllability-driven matrix selection, and an 8-state Bayesian chain with a latching point-of-no-return gate.
models.lifecycle_stage: Stage 2 complete - Models A-D and the end-to-end orchestrator built with unit tests; Stage 3 governance integration in progress
models.methodology: Initiation (Model A): lambda_i = lambda_0,c * m_occ * m_proc * m_cond * m_protection * m_history; a fire instantiates for an asset-draw when the Poisson count N_i >= 1. Intensity track (Model B): I_{t+1} = I_t + g_t where g_t = growth_per_step * (1 - passive_damp_weight * passive_effectiveness), scaled by the suppression multiplier once suppression is active. Response effectiveness (Model C): maps CDM resilience levels to detection time, suppression-bite time (with a storey-based height penalty), growth rate, critical threshold and an aggregate controllability score, and maps the structural-frame ConstructionType to a combustibility fraction. Combustibility drives the conflagration leg three ways: (1) it scales the per-step intensity growth (the timing leg — a combustible frame catches faster, leaving suppression less time to win the race); (2) it sets a fuel cap (intensity ceiling) on the latent intensity, with a small per-fire jitter so a non-combustible frame with no effective suppression keeps a small residual 'eventually it catches' conflagration chance rather than being absolutely immune; (3) it gates the unreachable-suppression auto-PNR latch and floors the containment-matrix blend weight (a non-combustible structure contains the fire passively even when active suppression cannot reach it). Containment (Model D): each 15-minute step selects a row-stochastic 8x8 transition matrix from the controllability score and the structural-containment floor (pre-PNR) or the absorbing point-of-no-return matrix (post-PNR), and samples the state until an absorbing terminal state {Contained, PartialLoss, TotalLoss} is reached or the step budget runs out. The point of no return latches when latent intensity (capped at the combustibility ceiling) exceeds the critical threshold before suppression bites, or when suppression is structurally unreachable AND the frame is combustible; a non-combustible frame (e.g. reinforced concrete, steel) plateaus below the threshold and so resists a full conflagration regardless of height or suppression. Aggregated into loss_frequency = (n_partial + n_total) / n_sim and containment_rate = n_contained / n_fires.
alternatives_considered: Continuous coupled-ODE intensity/suppression formulation (rejected for the first build: harder to calibrate and govern than the discrete 8-state chain; the discrete chain was chosen to show one formulation working end-to-end).

Flat resilience-level list on AssetFireFeatures (rejected: Model C needs to read detection, suppression and the passive/response fields separately, so the features were refactored to named fields with a protection_levels convenience property).
models.methodology_rationale: An 8-state discrete-time Bayesian chain in 15-minute steps mirrors the storm Monte Carlo engine's event/step structure, keeps every transition probability an auditable governance artefact in config/fire_matrices.json, and makes the point-of-no-return an explicit, testable gate rather than an emergent ODE property.

assumptions.description: Structural-frame combustibility is a single fraction mapped from ConstructionType (config/fire_matrices.json construction.combustibility_by_type). It drives the growth-rate scaling, the intensity fuel cap (plus a per-fire ceiling jitter that sets the small residual conflagration tail for non-combustible frames) and the structural-containment credit. Non-combustible frames (reinforced concrete, steel, brick) plateau below the critical threshold and keep only a small residual conflagration chance; the threshold separating non-combustible from combustible frames, the placement of ambiguous categories (Modern methods seeded below the threshold and less combustible than Mixed construction, which stays above it), the growth-scale band and the ceiling-jitter sigma are engineering-judgement seeds, not calibrated. Combustibility is treated as a property of the frame only; combustible cladding over a non-combustible frame (the Grenfell case) is not yet modelled.

limitations.description: Fast chain absorption (~3 steps) mutes the time-dependent dynamics. Confirmed by the sensitivity tables: the conflagration / point-of-no-return leg is insensitive to the active suppression level (it responds chiefly to compartmentation and the fire-service-reach cliff); the automatic-detection sensitivity is near-flat (<1 percentage point of containment across all five levels); and the non-combustible ceiling-jitter residual realises as effectively zero (sub-bp), because the chain absorbs before the capped intensity can creep across i_crit. This is the doc's FIRE-L3 (numbering differs between the inventory and the LaTeX model document).

limitations.description: The conflagration leg prices every point-of-no-return event at a 100% loss-given-event, including the fires the absorbing matrix sends to partial (S6) rather than total (S7) loss. n_point_of_no_return counts partial- and total-loss fires alike but is priced at full total-loss severity, so the fire-spread bps overstates a severity-weighted leg (a conservative bias). This is the doc's FIRE-L6.
limitations.monitoring_trigger: Any pricing use of the fire-spread leg
limitations.compensating_control: Conservative (overstates rather than understates risk); a modelled partial/total severity split is tracked as remediation FIRE-R6

known_failure_modes: A transition-matrix row that sums to zero raises at sample time rather than silently absorbing (defensive renormalisation handles non-zero drift).

Very small n_sim gives noisy containment_rate / loss_frequency estimates.

models.name: Building Seismic-Resilience Credit Model
models.description: Prices the seismic resilience of a commercial asset so seismic loss aggregates into the same resilience-credit currency as the 10,000-storm engine and the fire model, and is consumed by the Commercial PRS Pricer as an independent leg combined with the flood, wind and fire legs through a root-sum-of-squares all-in coupon.
models.tier_rationale: Materiality TBD: the seismic-resilience credit feeds the PRS-priced coupon as an independent peril leg, but the model is on placeholder (seed-0) calibration, so the priced impact is directional, not absolute. Tier 2 reflects a multi-component hazard model that prices into the loan/PRS chain.
models.lifecycle_stage: Stages 0-8 complete - Models A-D (occurrence + fault-geometry spatial draw, GMPE, response effectiveness, lognormal fragility chain), the port stage, the PRS-pricer and Loan-Calculator integration, and the sensitivity harness (all Section 7.7 acceptance gates pass). Placeholder seed-0 calibration pending.
models.methodology: Four governance-separated component models. Model A (occurrence): a homogeneous Poisson process with per-asset rate lambda_i = lambda_zone * m_fault * m_soil; magnitude from the truncated Gutenberg-Richter law; rupture centroid sampled by arc-length along the catchment fault trace; Wells-Coppersmith rupture length; Joyner-Boore distance R_JB to the rupture. Model B (ground motion): a lognormal GMPE maps (M, R_JB, V_S30) to a site PGA, with a soft-soil F_a gate. Model C (response effectiveness): a deterministic mapping from the BRI geoseismic measures (GS01-GS18) to fragility-median multipliers, recovery acceleration and the post-earthquake-fire probability. Model D (damage): a single-step lognormal fragility draw assigns DS0-DS3, a loss draw gives the structural loss (DS3 = 100%), a conditional post-earthquake-fire cascade applies max(L_seismic, L_fire), and aggregation emits the seismic spread = n_DS3 / n_sim * 10,000 bps.
alternatives_considered: Full probabilistic-seismic-hazard logic-tree with an epistemic GMPE ensemble (rejected for the first build: harder to govern and calibrate than a single seeded GMPE; only the aleatory residual is sampled for now).

A site-only hazard lookup with no fault geometry (rejected: it cannot price source-to-site distance, which is a first-order driver; the fault-trace spatial draw reuses the storm river-centreline primitive instead).
models.methodology_rationale: The four-model PSHA/PBEE decomposition (Poisson occurrence with a fault-geometry spatial draw, GMPE intensity sampling, BRI measure -> modifier mapping, lognormal fragility with a loss draw) is the standard framework used in HAZUS, GEM and Eurocode 8 seismic risk assessment, and is a structural twin of the fire-resilience credit model so the two price pari-passu.

assumptions.description: Mainshock occurrence is a homogeneous Poisson process; an earthquake instantiates for a draw when N >= 1, and multiple events in one draw are collapsed to a single event.

assumptions.description: Fragility is a single-step lognormal function (the HAZUS/GEM/Eurocode 8 standard form); damage state is assigned from one uniform draw against the adjusted medians.
assumptions.monitoring: Benchmark damage-state distributions against published fragility curves
assumptions.mitigation: The lognormal form is the universally used convention

assumptions.mitigation: The seam is in place; the seed is a defensible high-mean draw

limitations.compensating_control: Construction class plus the GS measures carry the dominant fragility signal

known_failure_modes: Mis-tuned seeds can make the baseline (Moderate zone, 20 km) produce zero collapses, so the resilience sweep needs a near-fault condition to show differentiation (the sensitivity harness handles this).
Very small n_sim gives noisy seismic-spread / no-collapse estimates (1 bps ~ 2 collapses in 20,000 draws); the Section 7.7 gates apply a sampling-noise tolerance.
A fault trace shorter than the rupture length clips every rupture to the fault endpoints; intended for the sensitivity harness, but a real short fault would understate rupture extent.
key_parameters: lambda_zone, b-value, m_min, m_max per seismic hazard zone (config/seismic_zones.json)
GMPE coefficients (c0..c4, mref, vref, h, sigma_total) per tectonic regime

Fragility median PGA (DS1/DS2/DS3) and beta by construction class
BRI geoseismic measure modifiers delta_j (GS01-GS18) and the GS16-18 governance cap
Recovery acceleration r_acc by BRI rating and the GS18 uplift
Post-earthquake-fire cascade probabilities and the conditional fire-loss seed
